caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This is a nested donut chart displaying the percentage distribution of samples across two dimensions of ambiguity: sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring), with both rings segmented into categories labeled with their respective percentages. The outer ring, labeled “Ambiguity Std (Outer),” contains four segments: Std: 0.0 (49.0%, dark blue), Std: 0.47 (38.0%, medium blue), Std: 0.82 (7.0%, light blue), and Std: 0.94 (5.0%, very light blue). The inner ring, labeled “Max Ambiguity (Inner),” contains three segments: Max: 1 (39.0%, light blue), Max: 2 (47.7%, medium blue), and Max: 3 (14.2%, very light blue). Percentages are displayed directly inside each segment, and a legend to the right of the chart maps each color to its corresponding category for both rings. The segments are arranged in descending order of percentage within each ring, starting from the top-right and proceeding clockwise. No segments are exploded or visually emphasized beyond their color and labeled percentage.
